name: Völs
kurzbeschreibung: Vibrant market town on the western edge of Innsbruck, featuring the Schloß and a historic old town – urban yet close to nature.
beschreibung:
Overview

Völs is situated at an elevation of 574 meters in the Tyrolean Inn Valley directly bordering the western edge of Innsbruck in the district of Innsbruck-Land. The municipal territory extends from the southern banks of the Inn River across fertile valley plains to the wooded hill of the Blasiusberg and the foothills of the Mittelgebirge. Home to around 7,350 residents, Völs was officially granted market town status in the year 2000. To the south, the jagged limestone battlements of the Kalkkögel—often called the Dolomites of North Tyrol—frame the horizon, while the rugged precipices of the Karwendel Nordkette rise to the north. Völs masterfully pairs the conveniences of an urban hub with protected green sanctuaries such as the Völser Au wetlands and diverse recreational amenities.

History

The Blasiusberg hill represents one of the earliest continuously settled locations in the central Inn Valley: Neolithic stone axes, Urnfield burials, and a fortified Hallstatt hill settlement dating to around 500 BC confirm ancient human habitation. A fine Roman bronze weight shaped as a bust of Bacchus was uncovered during archaeological excavations in the village. Völs was first documented in 1188 as 'Velles'. The preeminent architectural landmark is the pilgrimage Church of Saint Blaise atop the Blasiusberg: recorded in 1286, the existing Baroque sanctuary was erected in 1733 and houses the famous bronze 'Black Cross' cast in 1522 by master bronze-caster Stephan Godl. For centuries, pilgrims have climbed the hill around Saint Blaise's feast day on February 3 to receive the traditional throat blessing. The village center preserves the historic Parish Church of Saints Jodok and Lucia, alongside the avant-garde Emmaus Church designed in 1967 by modernist architect Josef Lackner. Artifacts are exhibited at the Late Gothic Ansitz Thurnfels museum.

Getting There

By car, Völs is directly accessed via the Inntal Autobahn A12 at the Innsbruck-Kranebitten/Völs interchange or along the B171 state road in just a few minutes from downtown Innsbruck. Rail passengers benefit from Völs railway station on the Arlberg Railway: S-Bahn lines S1 and S2 as well as regional trains link the town to Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof in a rapid five to six minutes. In addition, Innsbruck IVB bus line T and regional VVT buses operate every ten minutes.

Tips

A stroll along the scenic Stations of the Cross path to the pilgrimage Church of Saint Blaise rewards walkers with panoramic perspectives over the Inn Valley, Innsbruck's skyline, and the Karwendel range. The Völser Badl leisure waterpark at the foot of the hill features competitive swimming pools, an 84-meter giant waterslide, and sunbathing lawns. Nature enthusiasts will appreciate the protected Völser Au riparian reserve along the Inn River, home to pristine floodplain forests and over 90 bird species alongside the Inn Cycle Path. Shoppers can explore the Cyta shopping district with over 100 specialty stores and eateries.
